name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Glenn Thompson with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: Thompson holds a heavily Republican seat, outspent Bilger more than 13-to-1, and prediction markets price his reelection at about 95%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Bilger within single digits would warrant a shift toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Glenn Thompson seeks another term in a north-central Pennsylvania district that leans about 19 points Republican. He has raised roughly $1.85 million and holds more than $800,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Ray Bilger has raised under $150,000 and has no measurable outside support. Prediction markets give Thompson about a 95 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

The forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture, since no public general-election polling is available. Thompson is a strong favorite, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
